description: Somos el equipo ALIADOS, apasionados por la integración de la tecnología espacial, el diseño y el análisis geoespacial para resolver desafíos socioambientales reales. Para el reto 'Bailando con los SAR', buscamos potenciar la interpretación de datos satelitales mediante programación, análisis y visualización técnica. Buscamos colaboradores con habilidades en Codificación (Python/GIS), Análisis de datos, Inteligencia artificial y Ciencias de la Tierra que quieran transformar datos de radar
summary: In the Ecuadorian Amazon, vital environmental data on rainfall, river flows, forest cover, and biodiversity is fragmented across multiple sources. This dispersion makes it difficult to track ecological changes, pinpoint affected areas, and correlate impacts with El Niño episodes—particularly in critical ecosystems like the Colonso–Chalupas Biological Reserve in Napo. Addressing NASA’s “Dancing with SAR” challenge, we developed NISAR Pulse, an interactive web platform using Colonso–Chalupas as a pilot case study. By integrating Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imagery with hydro-climatic and biodiversity records into a layered map and timeline, the platform centralizes scattered information, helps prioritize field inspections, and empowers communities and researchers to protect Amazonian forests and watersheds.
details:
What it does & how it works:
NISAR Pulse (https://marlonmiranda-dotcom.github.io/nisar-pulse/) is an interactive web platform designed to centralize environmental monitoring in the Ecuadorian Amazon, using the Colonso–Chalupas Biological Reserve in Napo as its first case study. The tool combines Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) satellite images with rainfall, temperature, and river flow data, alongside biodiversity records. Through an interactive layered map and a timeline, users can compare different areas and time periods to spot structural changes in the forest and watersheds.

Benefits & Intended Impact: Today, the platform makes it easier to look up scattered information in one place and helps prioritize which critical areas to check in the field. In the future, by adding new satellite and field observations, it will help distinguish one-time events (such as El Niño episodes) from long-term climate trends—guiding evidence-based decisions to conserve forests and protect water sources for Amazonian communities.

Creativity & Factors Considered: In the Amazon basin, persistent cloud cover limits traditional optical satellite monitoring. Our team accounted for this regional challenge by leveraging cloud-penetrating SAR radar data and connecting it directly with local hydro-climatic and biodiversity records, turning scattered scientific data into an accessible visual tool.

Tools & Technologies Used: Interactive web interface hosted on GitHub Pages (HTML, CSS, JavaScript), integrating NASA SAR satellite imagery, historical hydro-climatic series (rainfall, temperature, river flow), and geospatial biodiversity datasets.
